title: What If Jupiter Became a Star? It Falls Short by 80 Times

scenes.text: What if Jupiter became a star? It already holds twice the matter of everything else orbiting the Sun.
Not nearly enough. To fuse even a little, a brown dwarf starts around 13 Jupiter masses.
A small red dwarf star needs about 80 times Jupiter's mass.
A Sun-like star needs roughly 1,000 Jupiters stacked together.
That is why Jupiter is called a failed star. It is a giant, but far too light to ignite.
Even our biggest planet misses the smallest true star by a factor of 80.

description:
What if Jupiter became a star?
It holds more than twice the matter of all other solar system objects combined, yet it would need about 80 times more mass to become even a red dwarf.
